description: Catalogue a pcap or pcapng: capinfos metadata and a complete listing of the selected fields of every packet and of the DNS, HTTP and TLS packets (and of HTTP/2 and QUIC packets when the installed tshark lists their fields), for examiner pivots. A receipt from the first moment records each step, the tool versions and the truncated packets; the listings are one tshark's reading, not the capture. The row counts of finished listings are made under the recipe's own clock: a count it could not finish is null and the status is partial. A stop that arrives before the script's first line has run (the interpreter's own start and its compile of the script) gets no answer: SIGTERM at a random offset of 0-250 ms after the start, 80 runs on one CPU (2026-11-01), left 11 runs without JSON, the latest at 38 ms, on a quiet host; a busy host sees more (misses up to about 80 ms were seen). A process capinfos or tshark leaves behind after it exits (in the recipe's process group or in a session of its own, or one that holds no descriptor) is stopped, killed and reaped by the shared process block's settle() before the listings are counted; one found, or a host where the absence of one cannot be proven (not Linux, PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER refused), makes the status partial and says why in status_basis, and coverage.json carries program_group (left_behind, unproven).
exclusions: protocols other than DNS, HTTP, TLS, and HTTP/2 and QUIC where the installed tshark lists their fields, are listed per packet, not decoded field by field
payloads and transferred objects are not reassembled or carved
fields of packets that were truncated, malformed or of a protocol tshark does not decode
http2.tsv and quic.tsv are not made when the installed tshark does not list the fields they need (the receipt says so)
covers: Capture metadata and, for every packet, the selected fields tshark can decode (packets.tsv), with DNS, HTTP and TLS listings and, only where the installed tshark lists their fields, HTTP/2 and QUIC. It does not assert that a missing protocol is absent when packets were truncated, encrypted, malformed or unsupported; coverage.json counts the truncated packets. http.tsv, dns.tsv, tls.tsv and http2.tsv can hold credentials, tokens and names in request URIs, query names and server names and are marked secret-bearing in the receipt (the mark is informational: nothing in the harness reads it); the directory is private (0700, files 0600). A field the installed tshark does not list is named in the step and left out of that listing.
